summary: Focused confirmation pass for the iteration_131 follow-ups. (1) GAP FIX, the default align=right case: CONFIRMED FIXED end-to-end. Via the UI, typed 'الموضوع: طلب ترشيح' + 28 spaces + 'ABC DEF' into the subject box and 'وتقبلوا فائق الاحترام' + 28 spaces + 'ABC DEF' into the closing box (align right), captured the real preview-pdf payload and replayed it. pymupdf char-level positions show gaps of 114.5pt and 110.4pt between the Arabic and the Latin (previously ~4pt). BUT a 33-case matrix probe (draw_rich x-positions, 25 spaces vs 1 space) shows the gap is STILL LOST in 7 of 33 cases: (a) align=right or center with a 2+ word Latin run FIRST, then Arabic ('ABC DEF'+gap+'نص عربي', 'ABC DEF'+gap+'نص'); (b) align=left with a 2+ word Arabic run FIRST, then Latin ('نص عربي'+gap+'XYZ', 'نص عربي'+gap+'ABC DEF', 'الموضوع: طلب ترشيح'+gap+'ABC'). Case (b) was also confirmed end-to-end on the UI payload with align switched to left: max gap 4pt. iteration_131's own Example 1 ('نص عربي'+25sp+'XYZ' align=left) still fails in test_letters_custom_people.py. That is broader than the 'single isolated trailing word' limitation the main agent accepted: it happens for any align=left line that starts with 2+ Arabic words followed by Latin. Also, (a) is new and affects the default right alignment. (2) Custom person draft reload: CONFIRMED FIXED via UI. The chip keeps its id 'custom-<ts>' and the label 'TEST_يدوي_أ (رئيس اللجنة) (يدوي)'. Adding a 2nd manual person, removing the 1st and adding a 3rd all behave correctly, with 0 duplicate-key console warnings. The API roundtrip also keeps ids [custom-a1, custom-b2] and fields. (3) Dangling 'المستوى': CONFIRMED FIXED. A student's level was temporarily set to '' and then restored to 1. The student-only table has an empty المستوى cell, and the mixed table's القسم/الوظيفة cell is 'الشريعة والقانون' with no '— المستوى'. (4) Regression: test_letters_custom_people.py 10/11 pass (the only failure is the left-align gap case above). Leading-space and left-shift tests pass. Layout_sections/drafts/iter125 pass 21/24. The 3 failures are pre-existing (identical on HEAD~10), not from this round.

critical.issue: The manual multi-space gap is still collapsed to ~4pt at a bidi run boundary in 7 of 33 probed cases: align=right/center with 'ABC DEF'+25sp+'نص عربي' (a multi-word Latin run first), and align=left with 'نص عربي'+25sp+'XYZ' / 'ABC DEF' / 'الموضوع: طلب ترشيح'+25sp+'ABC' (a multi-word Arabic run first). The new directional branches pick w.sp or nxt.sp, but at the boundary the large gap belongs to a THIRD word: the logical word just before the boundary, which is not one of the two visual neighbours. Tested fix (monkeypatched in the probe only; source not changed): for visual neighbours with idx a and b where |a-b| != 1, set _draw_sp = max(sp of words with idx in range(min(a,b), max(a,b))). This makes all 33 cases pass, including the currently-OK ones.

critical_code_review_comments: _apply_draw_gaps only ever looks at w and nxt. At a reversed-run boundary the gap-carrying word is generally neither of them, which is why the directional ni>wi / wi>ni branches fix only some orderings. A range-based max(sp) over the logical span is simpler and covers every ordering.
The main agent's verification covered 3 orderings. Please use the matrix probe, which covers right/left/center × Arabic-first/Latin-first × 1-word/multi-word runs, to avoid partial fixes.

rca of the issue: Example: logical 'نص(0) عربي(1)' + gap(sp on idx1) + 'XYZ(2)' with align=left gives visual order [عربي(1), نص(0), XYZ(2)]. The neighbours at the boundary are نص(0) and XYZ(2), and the new branch ni>wi uses نص.sp (1 space). The 25-space gap is on عربي(1), which is not adjacent visually, so it is never drawn. The same happens with right align and 'ABC(0) DEF(1)'+gap+'نص(2) عربي(3)': the visual neighbours are ABC(0) and نص(2), while the gap sits on DEF(1). Fix: use the max sp over idx range [min, max).
